verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents internal status pages "meant for the internal team only." Each incident gets an ephemeral internal page that collects updates posted via Slack or Command Center, which covers the employee-only audience. Access control is thin: the docs only say these pages need no auth or license for incidents that are public to the organization, without describing auth gating for restricted incidents. The external pages (Atlassian and FireHydrant-hosted) have no documented private or customer-specific access controls. Missing for 10: documented access-control configuration (SSO/password/allowlist gating) for status pages, private customer-specific status pages for audience segments, persistent internal status pages beyond per-incident ephemeral ones, independent corroboration.
